Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-29.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. frame.process: A paper claim represents a fixed gold entitlement.
frame.how: The issuer returns gold when the holder presents the redeemable note.
frame.when: Under a historical gold-redemption arrangement, on demand.
frame.conditions: A credible fixed-gold redemption promise is required.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical bank counter, not today's Indian rupee system.

frame.process: Gold backing constrains additional note issue.
frame.how: Additional claims require supporting gold under the illustrative arrangement.
frame.when: Reserves support issue before redemption is demanded.
frame.conditions: The fully backed arithmetic is illustrative, not a historical reserve ratio.
frame.atmosphere: A bank balances gold stock against promised claims.

frame.process: Selected milestones trace paper claims, state authority and changing gold links.
frame.how: Chronological markers distinguish receipts, state notes, compulsory acceptance and monetary anchors.
frame.when: From Tang receipts in the 7th century to the 1971 endpoint.
frame.conditions: Geographical scope and official versus household redemption must remain distinct.
frame.atmosphere: Chinese and European developments join the international dollar-gold transition.

skipped_steps.why: The supplied milestones name authorities and arrangements but provide no individual decision-makers or choices.

frame.process: Fiat money supports purchases without commodity redemption.
frame.how: Government authority and confidence in continued acceptance support monetary value.
frame.when: A seller accepts payment expecting to spend it again.
frame.conditions: Material value, purchasing power and gold convertibility are different.
frame.atmosphere: A modern Indian kirana purchase.

frame.process: Fiat characteristics and currency examples identify value, governance and international use.
frame.how: Separate printing, authorised issuance and monetary-policy influence; identify currencies by codes.
frame.when: Modern fiat systems, with historical and undated captions qualified.
frame.conditions: No gold backing does not mean no regulation or no purchasing power.
frame.atmosphere: Indian monetary institutions and international currency markets.

skipped_steps.why: No formula is supplied for these characteristics or currency captions.

frame.process: Recognised currency settles obligations, with or without aggregate tender ceilings.
frame.how: Legal status and denomination determine payment capacity; circulation designs do not change denomination.
frame.when: Existing monetary obligations are settled using genuine, valid money.
frame.conditions: Applicable territory, legal rules and amount limits govern the result.
frame.atmosphere: Indian grocery debt settlements using notes and coins.

frame.process: Coin categories and denomination limits determine recognised payment use.
frame.how: Check issue status, total rupee value and whether acceptance is compulsory or voluntary.
frame.when: At payment; historical coins may retain collector value after losing tender status.
frame.conditions: Commemorative purpose does not establish universal tender status.
frame.atmosphere: A change drawer, Government Mint collector sets and an old household coin collection.

frame.process: Bitcoin illustrates changing legal payment status without sovereign fiat issuance.
frame.how: Legal recognition changes acceptance rules rather than the network's issuance system.
frame.when: The supplied account contrasts status through 2024 with practical changes after 2025 reforms.
frame.conditions: Ownership, voluntary use and compulsory acceptance must be distinguished.
frame.atmosphere: El-Salvador's dated Bitcoin example.

skipped_steps.why: No individual policymakers or personal choices are supplied.

frame.process: One coin carries different monetary and collector valuations.
frame.how: Payment uses denomination; a collector's voluntary purchase uses a market price.
frame.when: The coin is spent as money versus sold as a collectible.
frame.conditions: Collector premiums do not rewrite face value or aggregate tender limits.
frame.atmosphere: A valid ₹100 silver commemorative coin.

frame.process: Fee payments distinguish currency from instruments accessing deposits or credit.
frame.how: Successful cheque clearing transfers funds; card settlement creates repayment liability.
frame.when: Alternative routes for a hypothetical ₹1,000 fee.
frame.conditions: Acceptance arrangements and successful settlement are required.
frame.atmosphere: A college fee counter and the connected banking arrangements.

beats.say: सस्ते कागज़ का ₹100 note चावल क्यों दिलाता है? क्या gold ज़रूरी है? Payment में स्वीकार होना ही legal tender होना है?
beats.on_screen: ₹100 note → rice; backing versus legal status

beats.say: एक hypothetical पुराने bank में note लौटाएँ तो क्या मिले? Bank 1 gram gold देता है; आपके notes 1 से 0 और gold 0 से 1 gram हो जाता है। आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: holder returns 1 note and receives 1 gram gold; not today's rupee

beats.say: यह gold-backed paper currency है: माँगने पर तय gold मिले। Intrinsic value यानी material की कीमत; यहाँ value paper से नहीं, redemption promise से है, जैसे सामान की receipt।
beats.on_screen: Paper material ≠ redeemable gold claim

beats.say: सिर्फ bank का gold रखना काफी नहीं; note लौटाने पर gold मिलना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Gold assets alone ≠ redeemability

beats.say: Value gold claim से आई।
beats.on_screen: Gold claim supports value

beats.say: Bank के 10 grams से 10 notes के 1-gram claims पूरे होंगे। Fully backed उदाहरण में 11वाँ note जारी करे, तो gold 10 से 11 grams करना होगा।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative full backing: 10 notes / 10 grams → 11 notes / 11 grams

beats.say: यही gold-backing constraint है; gold reserves यानी claims पूरे करने का stock।
beats.on_screen: Reserves support redemption claims

beats.say: Central bank gold रखकर notes जारी करता था और माँगने पर तय gold देता था। इसलिए नए notes को backing चाहिए थी; redemption in principle था, हर जगह unrestricted नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserves → note issue → fixed-gold redemption; in principle

beats.say: Claims चुकाने की क्षमता घटे, तो भरोसा टूटे और लोग gold माँगें।
beats.on_screen: Unmeetable claims → redemption pressure

beats.say: हर note पर 1 gram सिर्फ उदाहरण है, historical reserve ratio नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration, not a historical reserve ratio

beats.say: Backing की ज़रूरत issue रोकती थी।
beats.on_screen: Backing requirement constrains issue

beats.say: सामान की जगह receipt चले तो? इतिहास में paper claims, सरकारी issue और acceptance rules अलग milestones बने।
beats.on_screen: Paper claim → state issue → acceptance rules

beats.say: जमा value का सबूत चाहिए तो receipt काम आती है; 7th century में Tang receipts यही paper-claim stage दिखाती हैं। 1023 के Song state notes में issuer सरकारी authority थी; अब पहचान सिर्फ claim की नहीं, जारी करने वाले की भी थी।
beats.on_screen: 7th c. Tang: written claim → 1023 Song: state issuer

beats.say: लोग note लेने से मना करें तो? 1275 का Yuan milestone compulsory acceptance है, यानी नियम से लेना ज़रूरी। Sweden के first banknotes 1661 में आए; इसे दुनिया की शुरुआत मत समझिए, Chinese developments पहले हुए।
beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: refusal versus compulsory acceptance → 1661 Sweden; earlier Chinese developments

beats.say: पैसे को fixed आधार कैसे मिले? Britain का 1816 Gold Standard पैसे के unit को तय gold से जोड़ता था। International exchange के common आधार के लिए 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link बना; official convertibility, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1816 Britain: currency unit → fixed gold; 1944: official dollar–gold link

beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences यहीं modern fiat era तक पहुँचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

beats.say: अब gold promise की जगह authority और trust से value समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold promise → authority and trust

beats.say: Paper claims से issuer, acceptance और gold का आधार बदलता गया।
beats.on_screen: Claims → state issue → acceptance rules → gold anchors → 1971 break

beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? खरीदने पर आपकी cash ₹100 से ₹0, उसकी receipt ₹0 से ₹100; भरोसा है, आगे वही note चलेगा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; seller ₹0 → ₹100 → next purchase

beats.say: यह fiat money है: value government authority और public trust से, material से नहीं। यानी आज मिला note कल groceries दिलाएगा।
beats.on_screen: Authority + continued acceptance, not material value

beats.say: Gold-backed paper का आधार redemption था; इसलिए हर paper note fiat नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Paper form ≠ fiat basis

beats.say: Fiat का आधार authority और trust है।
beats.on_screen: Authority + public trust

beats.say: Press से note निकलना और पैसा जारी होना क्या एक काम है? Fiat paper या digital numbers हो सकता है; face value gold-silver से नहीं बँधी, government authority, central-bank control और public trust से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Material value; commodity backing; authority; trust

beats.say: और issue संभव है, मगर monetary policy control करती है। Outside clarification: printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलने से कुल पैसा बढ़ना ज़रूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: additional issue possible, subject to monetary-policy regulation. Outside clarification: printing ≠ authorised issuance; replacement need not increase currency.

beats.say: Outside clarification: policy rates और liquidity से loan महँगा हो, तो दुकानदार expansion रोक सकता है। Borrowing और spending घटें, तो goods के मुकाबले demand और prices का दबाव घट सकता है। सस्ता credit उलटा असर कर सकता है; असर समय लेता है, missing goods नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Outside clarification — standard textbook mechanism: costlier credit → expansion postponed → borrowing/spending lower → less demand pressure relative to available goods → lower upward price pressure. Easier credit can reverse the chain. Transmission takes time; policy cannot immediately repair supply shortages.

beats.say: Foreign price tags में codes क्यों देखें? $ वाला United States Dollar, USD, सबसे widely held और traded fiat currency है। € यानी Euro, EUR, कई EU देशों की shared currency है।
beats.on_screen: $ USD: United States Dollar; € EUR: Euro

beats.say: ¥ Japan या China, कैसे पहचानेंगे? Japanese Yen, JPY, stability और global currency markets में बड़े role के लिए जाना जाता है। Chinese Yuan Renminbi, CNY, trade और international reserves में बढ़ रहा है, यानी बाहरी payments के लिए रखे foreign assets में।
beats.on_screen: Shared ¥ symbol → JPY / Japan versus CNY / China; reserves → assets held for external payments

beats.say: नाम पुराना हो तो backing भी वही रहेगी? £ वाला British Pound Sterling, GBP, आज की fiat currencies में सबसे पुराना है; जड़ें 8th century में हैं। जैसे दुकान का नाम रहे पर मालिक बदले, currency का नाम रह सकता है, backing बदल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: GBP: currency history reaches 8th century; continuity of name ≠ continuous fiat backing

beats.say: Euro का historical count 27 EU members में 20 adopters है, सभी नहीं; इसे आज की updated गिनती मत मानिए।
beats.on_screen: Historical count: 20 of 27; EU membership ≠ euro adoption

beats.say: इन descriptions से exact market shares या हमेशा stable exchange rate मत निकालिए। Currency की पुरानी पहचान लगातार fiat रहने का सबूत नहीं; Euro की ranking बिना measure तय नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Source-evidence annotations, not narration: USD caption supplies no numerical shares or data source. EUR caption ends at ‘second-most’; ranking measure unspecified. JPY caption supplies no exchange-rate series or stability measure. GBP caption supplies no supporting historical explanation or source. CNY caption supplies no shares, dates or trend series. Inference boundary: qualitative descriptions do not establish exact shares or permanent stability.

beats.say: Reserve holdings backing नहीं; ज़्यादा पैसा goods नहीं बढ़ाता, इसलिए demand supply से आगे निकले तो purchasing power घट सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Outside clarification: foreign-currency reserve use ≠ gold-redemption backing; gold assets alone ≠ convertibility. Additional money does not itself create goods: demand outpacing supply can raise prices and weaken purchasing power.

beats.say: ₹100 उधार valid currency से चुकाएँ तो? ₹100 देने पर debt ₹100 से ₹0; यहाँ सवाल legally recognised settlement का है।
beats.on_screen: Recognised ₹100 payment: debt ₹100 → ₹0

beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? ₹10 खरीद में दें: coins 1 से 0, unpaid amount ₹10 से ₹0; payment denomination पर हुई।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative special-design ₹10 coin → ₹10 purchase

beats.say: Bill ₹1,000 से ₹1,500 हो: 2 से 3 valid ₹500 notes दें, ceiling नहीं आती। ₹10 coins 100 से 101 हों: ₹1,000 से ₹1,010; ceiling के ऊपर acceptance मर्ज़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Notes: 2 → 3; coins: 100 → 101 crosses ₹1,000

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender यानी genuine, valid notes जोड़ते जाएँ, tender की कुल रकम की ceiling नहीं आती। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes का यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Stack genuine, valid listed banknotes beyond an amount marker: no aggregate tender ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। इससे बहुत भारी coin payment लेने की कानूनी ज़रूरत नहीं रहती।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling → voluntary acceptance beyond; Coinage Act, 2011

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट या नई sale का अधिकार नहीं। Voluntary acceptance legal status नहीं; valid coins की ceiling पार करना demonetization नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No universal retail compulsion; excess amount ≠ lost status

beats.say: पहले recognition, फिर notes की no-ceiling या coins की amount-limit जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → validity → ceiling

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint collector sets: proof finish / uncirculated condition → preservation

beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Change के डिब्बे में कौन-से coins हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 को जोड़कर ₹1,000 तक की tender limit है। 50 paise जोड़ें तो ₹10 तक; उससे छोटे coins जोड़ने से legal-tender payment नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Sort change drawer: listed rupee coins → ₹1,000 meter; 50 paise → ₹10 meter; smaller coins → no tender status

beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
Coinage Act, 2011 के limits में 50 paise अलग है: आधा रुपया, उससे नीचे नहीं। इसलिए पुराने 25 paise से इसे मत मिलाइए। Commemorative coins में ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; कोई numerical count भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Coinage Act limits: 50 paise has its own row; 25 paise falls below it; most ≠ all or a numerical count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। Outside clarification: नए bitcoin mining से network rules पर बनते हैं; price demand-supply से बनती है, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dated historical account: through 2024. Outside clarification — standard textbook explanation: decentralised network rules govern mining and issuance; buyers and sellers determine market price, not a sovereign fixed-value or redemption promise.

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; ownership और voluntary use legal रहे। दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment संभव है—यह ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: compulsion removed; legal ownership and voluntary use remain

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Silver + condition + collectability → premium; face value remains ₹100

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: Value, legal status और payment method अलग हैं। आगे: gold link बिना dollar की माँग क्यों?
beats.on_screen: Value basis ≠ legal status ≠ payment instrument; next: demand for dollars after the gold link

beats.say: सस्ते कागज़ का ₹100 note चावल क्यों दिलाता है? क्या gold ज़रूरी है? Payment में स्वीकार होना ही legal tender होना है?
beats.on_screen: ₹100 note → rice; backing versus legal status

beats.say: एक hypothetical पुराने bank में note लौटाएँ तो क्या मिले? Bank 1 gram gold देता है; आपके notes 1 से 0 और gold 0 से 1 gram हो जाता है। आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: holder returns 1 note and receives 1 gram gold; not today's rupee

beats.say: यह gold-backed paper currency है: माँगने पर तय gold मिले। Intrinsic value यानी material की कीमत; यहाँ value paper से नहीं, redemption promise से है, जैसे सामान की receipt।
beats.on_screen: Paper material ≠ redeemable gold claim

beats.say: सिर्फ bank का gold रखना काफी नहीं; note लौटाने पर gold मिलना चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Gold assets alone ≠ redeemability

beats.say: Value gold claim से आई।
beats.on_screen: Gold claim supports value

beats.say: Bank के 10 grams से 10 notes के 1-gram claims पूरे होंगे। Fully backed उदाहरण में 11वाँ note जारी करे, तो gold 10 से 11 grams करना होगा।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative full backing: 10 notes / 10 grams → 11 notes / 11 grams

beats.say: यही gold-backing constraint है; gold reserves यानी claims पूरे करने का stock।
beats.on_screen: Reserves support redemption claims

beats.say: Central bank gold रखकर notes जारी करता था और माँगने पर तय gold देता था। इसलिए नए notes को backing चाहिए थी; redemption in principle था, हर जगह unrestricted नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserves → note issue → fixed-gold redemption; in principle

beats.say: Claims चुकाने की क्षमता घटे, तो भरोसा टूटे और लोग gold माँगें।
beats.on_screen: Unmeetable claims → redemption pressure

beats.say: हर note पर 1 gram सिर्फ उदाहरण है, historical reserve ratio नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Illustration, not a historical reserve ratio

beats.say: Backing की ज़रूरत issue रोकती थी।
beats.on_screen: Backing requirement constrains issue

beats.say: सामान की जगह receipt चले तो? इतिहास में paper claims, सरकारी issue और acceptance rules अलग milestones बने।
beats.on_screen: Paper claim → state issue → acceptance rules

beats.say: जमा value का सबूत चाहिए तो receipt काम आती है; 7th century में Tang receipts यही paper-claim stage दिखाती हैं। 1023 के Song state notes में issuer सरकारी authority थी; अब पहचान सिर्फ claim की नहीं, जारी करने वाले की भी थी।
beats.on_screen: 7th c. Tang: written claim → 1023 Song: state issuer

beats.say: लोग note लेने से मना करें तो? 1275 का Yuan milestone compulsory acceptance है, यानी नियम से लेना ज़रूरी। Sweden के first banknotes 1661 में आए; इसे दुनिया की शुरुआत मत समझिए, Chinese developments पहले हुए।
beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: refusal versus compulsory acceptance → 1661 Sweden; earlier Chinese developments

beats.say: पैसे को fixed आधार कैसे मिले? Britain का 1816 Gold Standard पैसे के unit को तय gold से जोड़ता था। International exchange के common आधार के लिए 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link बना; official convertibility, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1816 Britain: currency unit → fixed gold; 1944: official dollar–gold link

beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences यहीं modern fiat era तक पहुँचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

beats.say: अब gold promise की जगह authority और trust से value समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold promise → authority and trust

beats.say: Paper claims से issuer, acceptance और gold का आधार बदलता गया।
beats.on_screen: Claims → state issue → acceptance rules → gold anchors → 1971 break

beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? खरीदने पर आपकी cash ₹100 से ₹0, उसकी receipt ₹0 से ₹100; भरोसा है, आगे वही note चलेगा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer ₹100 → ₹0; seller ₹0 → ₹100 → next purchase

beats.say: यह fiat money है: value government authority और public trust से, material से नहीं। यानी आज मिला note कल groceries दिलाएगा।
beats.on_screen: Authority + continued acceptance, not material value

beats.say: Gold-backed paper का आधार redemption था; इसलिए हर paper note fiat नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Paper form ≠ fiat basis

beats.say: Fiat का आधार authority और trust है।
beats.on_screen: Authority + public trust

beats.say: Press से note निकलना और पैसा जारी होना क्या एक काम है? Fiat paper या digital numbers हो सकता है; face value gold-silver से नहीं बँधी, government authority, central-bank control और public trust से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Material value; commodity backing; authority; trust

beats.say: और issue संभव है, मगर monetary policy control करती है। Outside clarification: printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलने से कुल पैसा बढ़ना ज़रूरी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: additional issue possible, subject to monetary-policy regulation. Outside clarification: printing ≠ authorised issuance; replacement need not increase currency.

beats.say: Outside clarification: policy rates और liquidity से loan महँगा हो, तो दुकानदार expansion रोक सकता है। Borrowing और spending घटें, तो goods के मुकाबले demand और prices का दबाव घट सकता है। सस्ता credit उलटा असर कर सकता है; असर समय लेता है, missing goods नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Costlier credit → expansion postponed → lower borrowing and spending → less demand pressure relative to available goods → lower upward price pressure. Easier credit can reverse the chain. Transmission takes time; policy cannot immediately repair supply shortages.

beats.say: Foreign price tags में codes क्यों देखें? $ वाला United States Dollar, USD, सबसे widely held और traded fiat currency है। € यानी Euro, EUR, कई EU देशों की shared currency है।
beats.on_screen: $ USD: United States Dollar; € EUR: Euro

beats.say: ¥ Japan या China, कैसे पहचानेंगे? Japanese Yen, JPY, stability और global currency markets में बड़े role के लिए जाना जाता है। Chinese Yuan Renminbi, CNY, trade और international reserves में बढ़ रहा है, यानी बाहरी payments के लिए रखे foreign assets में।
beats.on_screen: Shared ¥ symbol → JPY / Japan versus CNY / China; reserves → assets held for external payments

beats.say: नाम पुराना हो तो backing भी वही रहेगी? £ वाला British Pound Sterling, GBP, आज की fiat currencies में सबसे पुराना है; जड़ें 8th century में हैं। जैसे दुकान का नाम रहे पर मालिक बदले, currency का नाम रह सकता है, backing बदल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: GBP: currency history reaches 8th century; continuity of name ≠ continuous fiat backing

beats.say: Euro का historical count 27 EU members में 20 adopters है, सभी नहीं; इसे आज की updated गिनती मत मानिए।
beats.on_screen: Historical count: 20 of 27; EU membership ≠ euro adoption

beats.say: इन descriptions से exact market shares या हमेशा stable exchange rate मत निकालिए। Currency की पुरानी पहचान लगातार fiat रहने का सबूत नहीं; Euro की ranking बिना measure तय नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative importance ≠ exact market share. Stability ≠ permanently fixed exchange rate. Currency age ≠ duration of fiat status. Rankings require a specified measure. Increasing influence ≠ a quantified growth rate.

beats.say: Reserve holdings backing नहीं; ज़्यादा पैसा goods नहीं बढ़ाता, इसलिए demand supply से आगे निकले तो purchasing power घट सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Outside clarification: foreign-currency reserve use ≠ gold-redemption backing; gold assets alone ≠ convertibility. Additional money does not itself create goods: demand outpacing supply can raise prices and weaken purchasing power.

beats.say: ₹100 उधार valid currency से चुकाएँ तो? ₹100 देने पर debt ₹100 से ₹0; यहाँ सवाल legally recognised settlement का है।
beats.on_screen: Recognised ₹100 payment: debt ₹100 → ₹0

beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? ₹10 खरीद में दें: coins 1 से 0, unpaid amount ₹10 से ₹0; payment denomination पर हुई।
beats.on_screen: Illustrative special-design ₹10 coin → ₹10 purchase

beats.say: Bill ₹1,000 से ₹1,500 हो: 2 से 3 valid ₹500 notes दें, ceiling नहीं आती। ₹10 coins 100 से 101 हों: ₹1,000 से ₹1,010; ceiling के ऊपर acceptance मर्ज़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Notes: 2 → 3; coins: 100 → 101 crosses ₹1,000

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender यानी genuine, valid notes जोड़ते जाएँ, tender की कुल रकम की ceiling नहीं आती। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes का यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Stack genuine, valid listed banknotes beyond an amount marker: no aggregate tender ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। इससे बहुत भारी coin payment लेने की कानूनी ज़रूरत नहीं रहती।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling → voluntary acceptance beyond; Coinage Act, 2011

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट या नई sale का अधिकार नहीं। Voluntary acceptance legal status नहीं; valid coins की ceiling पार करना demonetization नहीं।
beats.on_screen: No universal retail compulsion; excess amount ≠ lost status

beats.say: पहले recognition, फिर notes की no-ceiling या coins की amount-limit जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Recognition → validity → ceiling

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint collector sets: proof finish / uncirculated condition → preservation

beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Change के डिब्बे में कौन-से coins हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 को जोड़कर ₹1,000 तक की tender limit है। 50 paise जोड़ें तो ₹10 तक; उससे छोटे coins जोड़ने से legal-tender payment नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Sort change drawer: listed rupee coins → ₹1,000 meter; 50 paise → ₹10 meter; smaller coins → no tender status

beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
Coinage Act, 2011 के limits में 50 paise अलग है: आधा रुपया, उससे नीचे नहीं। इसलिए पुराने 25 paise से इसे मत मिलाइए। Commemorative coins में ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; कोई numerical count भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Coinage Act limits: 50 paise has its own row; 25 paise falls below it; most ≠ all or a numerical count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। Outside clarification: नए bitcoin mining से network rules पर बनते हैं; price demand-supply से बनती है, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: El-Salvador: historical status through 2024. Decentralised network rules govern mining and issuance. Buyers and sellers determine market price; no sovereign fixed-value or redemption promise. Legal recognition and issuance remain separate attributes.

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; ownership और voluntary use legal रहे। दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment संभव है—यह ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: compulsion removed; legal ownership and voluntary use remain

beats.say: Recognition से network issuance सरकारी नहीं बनती; यह पूरा statutory account भी नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Changed legal recognition ≠ changed issuer

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Silver + condition + collectability → premium; face value remains ₹100

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: ₹1,000 fees का cheque currency बन गया? Clearing हो तो student deposit ₹2,000 से ₹1,000, college ₹0 से ₹1,000। Funds कम हों तो transfer नहीं, fees बाकी।
beats.on_screen: Successful cheque clearing transfers existing deposits; failed clearing leaves fees due

beats.say: Alternative credit-card route में issuer arrangement से college को settlement मिलता है; charges छोड़कर student का card debt ₹0 से ₹1,000। यहाँ existing deposit का instruction नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: Alternative card route: student debt ₹0 → ₹1,000

beats.say: ये payment instruments हैं: cheque bank को instruction, card credit तक पहुँच। Accepted payment method होने से वे खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनते; fiat value का आधार है, legal tender कानूनी status।
beats.on_screen: Instrument ≠ currency; acceptance ≠ legal-tender status

beats.say: Value, legal status और payment method अलग हैं। आगे: gold link बिना dollar की माँग क्यों?
beats.on_screen: Value basis ≠ legal status ≠ payment instrument; next: demand for dollars after the gold link

problems.problem: The required example-first sequence is broken. Legal tender is named in the hook before its debt-settlement example; fiat is named in the timeline before the kirana example. Cheque and credit card are named before their numerical routes run. Several examples also report account states rather than narrating what the actors did.
problems.fix: Use plain questions about acceptance and value before introducing the labels. Run the relevant transactions first, narrating the customer handing over money, the bank transferring ₹1,000 and the issuer settling payment; then name the concepts. Replace existing state-reporting lines and repetitive recaps rather than adding time.

problems.problem: Examinable outside explanations have no named dated sources. 'Outside clarification' identifies their status but does not satisfy S2-10. Other mixed beats do not clearly distinguish their outside additions, including official Bretton Woods convertibility and qualifications to compulsory acceptance.
problems.fix: Attach named, dated authoritative sources to retained examinable additions and clearly mark the outside portions of mixed beats. Cut optional outside detail or repeated recaps to accommodate concise attribution; retain all book content.

problems.problem: The definition pattern's final step is largely replaced by another summary. These beats repeat the meaning instead of explaining where the newly defined concept is used next. The circulation-commemorative definition also lacks a clear boundary test distinguishing it from a collector issue.
problems.fix: Replace the repeated summaries with explicit forward uses: redemption explains the issuance constraint; fiat characteristics explain governance without gold backing; legal-tender recognition leads to denomination-specific limits. Use the existing collector-set contrast to test whether a commemorative design alone establishes circulation use.

problems.problem: The cause-effect teaching pattern is not fully performed. The part opens with backing arithmetic rather than a visible problem or question, and its ending does not run the causal chain once at speed. Step labels alone do not establish the required teaching.
problems.fix: Open by asking whether the bank can issue an eleventh redeemable note without more gold. Replace b7/b11 repetition with one short causal run: promised gold creates redemption claims, claims require supporting reserves, so additional issue is constrained.

problems.problem: The maker's notes describe successive editing operations rather than the unit's teaching decisions and unresolved source limitations.
problems.fix: Summarise the conceptual distinctions, reasons for qualifying the historical captions, and uncertainty arising from undated or shorthand source claims.

replace_beats.say: सस्ते कागज़ का ₹100 note चावल क्यों दिलाता है? क्या gold ज़रूरी है? और किसी चीज़ को payment में लेना, क्या उसकी कानूनी मान्यता भी बताता है?
replace_beats.on_screen: Material value | backing | acceptance | legal recognition

replace_beats.say: एक पुराने hypothetical bank में note लौटाएँ तो क्या मिले? आपके पास 1 note है; bank उसे लेकर 1 gram gold देता है। अब note नहीं, gold आपके हाथ में है; आज का rupee ऐसा नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Historical illustration: return 1 note → receive 1 gram gold; not today's rupee

replace_beats.say: यह gold-backed paper currency है: माँगने पर तय gold मिले। Intrinsic value यानी material की कीमत; यहाँ value paper से नहीं, redemption promise से है, जैसे सामान की receipt।
replace_beats.on_screen: Paper material ≠ redeemable gold claim

replace_beats.say: सिर्फ bank के पास gold होना काफी नहीं; note पर gold पाने का claim चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Gold assets alone ≠ gold-redemption claim
replace_beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014

replace_beats.say: यह redemption promise आगे समझाएगा कि नए notes के लिए backing क्यों चाहिए।
replace_beats.on_screen: Redemption promise → next: constraint on note issue

replace_beats.say: Bank बिना और gold रखे 11वाँ note निकाल दे तो? मानिए, उसने 10 grams रखकर 10 notes दिए, हर note पर 1 gram का वादा। Fully backed उदाहरण में अगला note देने के लिए 1 gram और रखना होगा।
replace_beats.on_screen: 10 grams support 10 illustrative claims; an eleventh fully backed claim needs another gram

replace_beats.say: यही gold-backing constraint है; gold reserves यानी वादा पूरा करने का रखा हुआ gold।
replace_beats.on_screen: Gold reserves: stock available to honour redemption

replace_beats.say: Claims चुकाने की क्षमता घटे, तो भरोसा टूटे और लोग gold माँगें।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside explanation: unmeetable claims → loss of confidence → redemption pressure
replace_beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014

replace_beats.say: फिर देखिए: gold का वादा claim बनाता है; claims को reserves चाहिए; इसलिए नया issue बँधता है। 1 gram सिर्फ उदाहरण है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Promise → claims → supporting reserves → constrained issue; illustrative quantities

replace_beats.say: याद रखिए: issue के पीछे redemption की ज़िम्मेदारी थी।
replace_beats.on_screen: Note issue carries a redemption obligation

replace_beats.say: पैसे का fixed आधार कैसे बने? Britain का 1816 Gold Standard पैसे को तय gold से जोड़ता था। 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link आया; एक फर्क समझिए: official convertibility थी, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: 1816 Britain: Gold Standard; 1944 Bretton Woods: dollar–gold link. Outside clarification: official convertibility ≠ universal household redemption
replace_beats.source: Federal Reserve History, Creation of the Bretton Woods System, 2013

replace_beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences इसी modern दौर पर पहुँचते हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

replace_beats.say: अब सवाल है: gold देने का वादा नहीं, तो लोग note क्यों लेंगे?
replace_beats.on_screen: Without gold redemption, what supports acceptance?

replace_beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? आपके पास ₹100 हैं; सारे उसे देकर चावल लेते हैं। उसे ₹100 मिलते हैं, क्योंकि भरोसा है कि आगे वह भी इन्हें खर्च करेगा।
replace_beats.on_screen: Buyer hands over ₹100 for rice → seller accepts → seller can make a later payment

replace_beats.say: Authority और trust वाला यही आधार आगे समझाएगा: gold बिना issue कैसे control होता है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Fiat basis → next: issuance and monetary-policy governance

replace_beats.say: और issue संभव है, मगर monetary policy control करती है। एक फर्क समझिए: printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलना कुल पैसा बढ़ाना नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Book concepts: further issue and monetary-policy regulation. Outside clarification: printing ≠ authorised issuance; replacement need not expand currency

replace_beats.say: Policy rates और liquidity से loan महँगा हो, तो दुकानदार expansion टाल सकता है। Borrowing और spending घटें, तो prices का दबाव घट सकता है; सस्ता credit उलटा असर करे। असर समय लेता है, missing goods नहीं बनाता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside explanation: rates/liquidity → borrowing conditions → spending → price pressure; transmission takes time and cannot directly create missing supply

replace_beats.say: Reserve holdings backing नहीं; ज़्यादा पैसा goods नहीं बढ़ाता। Demand supply से आगे निकले तो purchasing power घट सकती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside clarification: reserve assets ≠ redemption promise; demand outpacing supply can weaken purchasing power
replace_beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014; RBI, Monetary Policy Report, April 2024

replace_beats.say: दुकान का ₹100 उधार कैसे चुकाएँ? आप ₹100 की valid currency देते हैं; दुकानदार payment लेकर पूरा उधार चुका मानता है। अब कुछ बाकी नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer pays recognised ₹100 currency → existing ₹100 debt cleared

replace_beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? आपके पास ऐसा 1 coin है; उसे देकर ₹10 की चीज़ लेते हैं। Coin दुकानदार को मिला, आपकी पूरी रकम चुक गई।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer hands over one illustrative valid ₹10 special-design coin → ₹10 purchase paid

replace_beats.say: ₹1,000 bill के लिए आप 2 valid ₹500 notes देते हैं; ₹1,500 हो तो 3 दे सकते हैं। लेकिन 100 ₹10 coins देकर ₹1,000 चुकाएँ, फिर 101 देकर ₹1,010 देना चाहें, तो limit के ऊपर लेना मर्ज़ी है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Existing bills: two or three ₹500 notes; compare 100 versus 101 ₹10 coins at the ₹1,000 ceiling

replace_beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। यानी बड़ा coin ढेर लेने की मजबूरी limit पर रुकती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling bounds compulsory acceptance; beyond it acceptance is voluntary

replace_beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट नहीं। और खास design से circulation साबित नहीं होता: collector set रोज़ चलने वाला coin नहीं। Valid coins की limit पार करना उनका status खोना नहीं है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside boundaries: legal-tender status ≠ unrestricted transactions or universal retail compulsion. Special design alone ≠ circulation issue; exceeding a ceiling ≠ demonetization
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Currency Management, 2024; Coinage Act, 2011, section 6; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 269ST, inserted 2017

replace_beats.say: Recognition के बाद अगला सवाल denomination और total limit है: notes की ceiling नहीं, coins की तय है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Legal recognition → next: denomination-specific aggregate limits

replace_beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। इसका mechanism अलग समझिए: नए bitcoin mining से network rules पर बनते हैं; price demand-supply से, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Historical example: El-Salvador through 2024. Outside explanation: protocol-governed mining; market valuation rather than a sovereign fixed-value promise
replace_beats.source: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, 2008; IMF, Global Financial Stability Report, Chapter 2, October 2021

replace_beats.say: कानूनी recognition बदलने से network का issuer government नहीं बनता।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside distinction: changed payment status ≠ sovereign issuance
replace_beats.source: IMF, Cryptoassets as National Currency? A Step Too Far, 2021

replace_beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside explanation: metal and collector attributes can produce a premium without changing face value
replace_beats.source: United States Mint, Coin Collecting Basics, 2024

replace_beats.say: College की ₹1,000 fees बिना cash कैसे भरें? आपके खाते में ₹2,000 हैं; आप bank को ₹1,000 देने का लिखा instruction देते हैं। Clearing पर bank college को ₹1,000 पहुँचाता है; आपके ₹1,000 बचते हैं। Funds कम हों तो fees बाकी रहती है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Written instruction → successful clearing transfers ₹1,000 from a ₹2,000 deposit → ₹1,000 remains; failed clearing leaves fee unpaid
replace_beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, sections 6 and 31; RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems, 2024

replace_beats.say: दूसरे रास्ते में issuer college को arrangement से payment पहुँचाता है। पहले आपका उससे कोई उधार नहीं था; अब ₹1,000 उसे लौटाने हैं, charges छोड़कर। आपने जमा पैसा नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल किया।
replace_beats.on_screen: Alternative route: issuer settles college payment → student owes issuer ₹1,000; charges and timing simplified
replace_beats.source: RBI, Credit Card and Debit Card—Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022

replace_beats.say: पहला cheque था, दूसरा credit card: दोनों payment instruments हैं। Cheque जमा पैसे का instruction है; card credit तक पहुँच है। College का लेना इन्हें खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनाता; value का आधार, legal status और payment method अलग हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Cheque: deposit-payment instruction; credit card: access to credit. Accepted instrument ≠ fiat currency or legal-tender status
replace_beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, section 6; RBI, Credit Card and Debit Card—Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022; Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, section 26

frame.process: A paper claim represents a fixed gold entitlement.
frame.how: The issuer returns gold when the holder presents the redeemable note.
frame.when: Under a historical gold-redemption arrangement, on demand.
frame.conditions: A credible fixed-gold redemption promise is required.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical bank counter, not today's Indian rupee system.

frame.process: Gold backing constrains additional note issue.
frame.how: Additional claims require supporting gold under the illustrative arrangement.
frame.when: Reserves support issue before redemption is demanded.
frame.conditions: The fully backed arithmetic is illustrative, not a historical reserve ratio.
frame.atmosphere: A bank balances gold stock against promised claims.

frame.process: Selected milestones trace paper claims, state authority and changing gold links.
frame.how: Chronological markers distinguish receipts, state notes, compulsory acceptance and monetary anchors.
frame.when: From Tang receipts in the 7th century to the 1971 endpoint.
frame.conditions: Geographical scope and official versus household redemption must remain distinct.
frame.atmosphere: Chinese and European developments join the international dollar-gold transition.

skipped_steps.why: The supplied milestones name authorities and arrangements but provide no individual decision-makers or choices.

frame.process: Fiat money supports purchases without commodity redemption.
frame.how: Government authority and confidence in continued acceptance support monetary value.
frame.when: A seller accepts payment expecting to spend it again.
frame.conditions: Material value, purchasing power and gold convertibility are different.
frame.atmosphere: A modern Indian kirana purchase.

frame.process: Fiat characteristics and currency examples identify value, governance and international use.
frame.how: Separate printing, authorised issuance and monetary-policy influence; identify currencies by codes.
frame.when: Modern fiat systems, with historical and undated captions qualified.
frame.conditions: No gold backing does not mean no regulation or no purchasing power.
frame.atmosphere: Indian monetary institutions and international currency markets.

skipped_steps.why: No formula is supplied for these characteristics or currency captions.

frame.process: Recognised currency settles obligations, with or without aggregate tender ceilings.
frame.how: Legal status and denomination determine payment capacity; circulation designs do not change denomination.
frame.when: Existing monetary obligations are settled using genuine, valid money.
frame.conditions: Applicable territory, legal rules and amount limits govern the result.
frame.atmosphere: Indian grocery debt settlements using notes and coins.

frame.process: Coin categories and denomination limits determine recognised payment use.
frame.how: Check issue status, total rupee value and whether acceptance is compulsory or voluntary.
frame.when: At payment; historical coins may retain collector value after losing tender status.
frame.conditions: Commemorative purpose does not establish universal tender status.
frame.atmosphere: A change drawer, Government Mint collector sets and an old household coin collection.

frame.process: Bitcoin illustrates changing legal payment status without sovereign fiat issuance.
frame.how: Legal recognition changes acceptance rules rather than the network's issuance system.
frame.when: The supplied account contrasts status through 2024 with practical changes after 2025 reforms.
frame.conditions: Ownership, voluntary use and compulsory acceptance must be distinguished.
frame.atmosphere: El-Salvador's dated Bitcoin example.

skipped_steps.why: No individual policymakers or personal choices are supplied.

frame.process: One coin carries different monetary and collector valuations.
frame.how: Payment uses denomination; a collector's voluntary purchase uses a market price.
frame.when: The coin is spent as money versus sold as a collectible.
frame.conditions: Collector premiums do not rewrite face value or aggregate tender limits.
frame.atmosphere: A valid ₹100 silver commemorative coin.

frame.process: Fee payments distinguish currency from instruments accessing deposits or credit.
frame.how: Successful cheque clearing transfers funds; card settlement creates repayment liability.
frame.when: Alternative routes for a hypothetical ₹1,000 fee.
frame.conditions: Acceptance arrangements and successful settlement are required.
frame.atmosphere: A college fee counter and the connected banking arrangements.

beats.say: लोग note लेने से मना करें तो? 1275 का Yuan milestone compulsory acceptance है, यानी नियम से लेना ज़रूरी। Sweden के first banknotes 1661 में आए; इसे दुनिया की शुरुआत मत समझिए, Chinese developments पहले हुए।
beats.on_screen: 1275 Yuan: refusal versus compulsory acceptance → 1661 Sweden; earlier Chinese developments

beats.say: पैसे का fixed आधार कैसे बने? Britain का 1816 Gold Standard पैसे को तय gold से जोड़ता था। 1944 Bretton Woods में dollar-gold link आया; एक फर्क समझिए: official convertibility थी, हर व्यक्ति का gold counter नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 1816 Britain: Gold Standard; 1944 Bretton Woods: dollar–gold link. Outside clarification: official convertibility ≠ universal household redemption
beats.source: Federal Reserve History, Creation of the Bretton Woods System, 2013

beats.say: 1971 में gold-redemption link टूटा; दोनों historical sequences इसी modern दौर पर पहुँचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Both historical sequences converge at 1971: no gold redemption

beats.say: अब सवाल है: gold देने का वादा नहीं, तो लोग note क्यों लेंगे?
beats.on_screen: Without gold redemption, what supports acceptance?

beats.say: Paper claims से issuer, acceptance और gold का आधार बदलता गया।
beats.on_screen: Claims → state issue → acceptance rules → gold anchors → 1971 break

beats.say: दुकानदार ₹100 note लेकर चावल क्यों दे? आपके पास ₹100 हैं; सारे उसे देकर चावल लेते हैं। उसे ₹100 मिलते हैं, क्योंकि भरोसा है कि आगे वह भी इन्हें खर्च करेगा।
beats.on_screen: Buyer hands over ₹100 for rice → seller accepts → seller can make a later payment

beats.say: यह fiat money है: value government authority और public trust से, material से नहीं। यानी आज मिला note कल groceries दिलाएगा।
beats.on_screen: Authority + continued acceptance, not material value

beats.say: Gold-backed paper का आधार redemption था; इसलिए हर paper note fiat नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Paper form ≠ fiat basis

beats.say: Authority और trust वाला यही आधार आगे समझाएगा: gold बिना issue कैसे control होता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat basis → next: issuance and monetary-policy governance

beats.say: Press से note निकलना और पैसा जारी होना क्या एक काम है? Fiat paper या digital numbers हो सकता है; face value gold-silver से नहीं बँधी, government authority, central-bank control और public trust से जुड़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Material value; commodity backing; authority; trust

beats.say: और issue संभव है, मगर monetary policy control करती है। एक फर्क समझिए: printing notes बनाती है; authorised issuance circulation में लाता है। पुराने notes बदलना कुल पैसा बढ़ाना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Book concepts: further issue and monetary-policy regulation. Outside clarification: printing ≠ authorised issuance; replacement need not expand currency
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Currency Management, 2024

beats.say: Policy rates और liquidity से loan महँगा हो, तो दुकानदार expansion टाल सकता है। Borrowing और spending घटें, तो prices का दबाव घट सकता है; सस्ता credit उलटा असर करे। असर समय लेता है, missing goods नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Outside explanation: rates/liquidity → borrowing conditions → spending → price pressure; transmission takes time and cannot directly create missing supply
beats.source: RBI, Monetary Policy Report, April 2024

beats.say: Foreign price tags में codes क्यों देखें? $ वाला United States Dollar, USD, सबसे widely held और traded fiat currency है। € यानी Euro, EUR, कई EU देशों की shared currency है।
beats.on_screen: $ USD: United States Dollar; € EUR: Euro

beats.say: ¥ Japan या China, कैसे पहचानेंगे? Japanese Yen, JPY, stability और global currency markets में बड़े role के लिए जाना जाता है। Chinese Yuan Renminbi, CNY, trade और international reserves में बढ़ रहा है, यानी बाहरी payments के लिए रखे foreign assets में।
beats.on_screen: Shared ¥ symbol → JPY / Japan versus CNY / China; reserves → assets held for external payments

beats.say: नाम पुराना हो तो backing भी वही रहेगी? £ वाला British Pound Sterling, GBP, आज की fiat currencies में सबसे पुराना है; जड़ें 8th century में हैं। जैसे दुकान का नाम रहे पर मालिक बदले, currency का नाम रह सकता है, backing बदल सकती है।
beats.on_screen: GBP: currency history reaches 8th century; continuity of name ≠ continuous fiat backing

beats.say: Euro का historical count 27 EU members में 20 adopters है, सभी नहीं; इसे आज की updated गिनती मत मानिए।
beats.on_screen: Historical count: 20 of 27; EU membership ≠ euro adoption

beats.say: इन descriptions से exact market shares या हमेशा stable exchange rate मत निकालिए। Currency की पुरानी पहचान लगातार fiat रहने का सबूत नहीं; Euro की ranking बिना measure तय नहीं होती।
beats.on_screen: Qualitative importance ≠ exact market share. Stability ≠ permanently fixed exchange rate. Currency age ≠ duration of fiat status. Rankings require a specified measure. Increasing influence ≠ a quantified growth rate.

beats.say: Reserve holdings backing नहीं; ज़्यादा पैसा goods नहीं बढ़ाता। Demand supply से आगे निकले तो purchasing power घट सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Outside clarification: reserve assets ≠ redemption promise; demand outpacing supply can weaken purchasing power
beats.source: Bank of England, Money in the modern economy: an introduction, 2014; RBI, Monetary Policy Report, April 2024

beats.say: दुकान का ₹100 उधार कैसे चुकाएँ? आप ₹100 की valid currency देते हैं; दुकानदार payment लेकर पूरा उधार चुका मानता है। अब कुछ बाकी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Customer pays recognised ₹100 currency → existing ₹100 debt cleared

beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? आपके पास ऐसा 1 coin है; उसे देकर ₹10 की चीज़ लेते हैं। Coin दुकानदार को मिला, आपकी पूरी रकम चुक गई।
beats.on_screen: Customer hands over one illustrative valid ₹10 special-design coin → ₹10 purchase paid

beats.say: ₹1,000 bill के लिए आप 2 valid ₹500 notes देते हैं; ₹1,500 हो तो 3 दे सकते हैं। लेकिन 100 ₹10 coins देकर ₹1,000 चुकाएँ, फिर 101 देकर ₹1,010 देना चाहें, तो limit के ऊपर लेना मर्ज़ी है।
beats.on_screen: Existing bills: two or three ₹500 notes; compare 100 versus 101 ₹10 coins at the ₹1,000 ceiling

beats.say: Legal tender यानी territory में debts और transactions चुकाने के लिए government से officially recognised money। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने coins हैं, जो रोज़ के payments में ordinary coins जैसे चलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

beats.say: Unlimited Legal Tender यानी genuine, valid notes जोड़ते जाएँ, tender की कुल रकम की ceiling नहीं आती। ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200, ₹500 notes का यह status Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 से जुड़ा है।
beats.on_screen: Stack genuine, valid listed banknotes beyond an amount marker: no aggregate tender ceiling; RBI Act, 1934

beats.say: Limited Legal Tender में तय amount तक लेना ज़रूरी, आगे मर्ज़ी है; coins के लिए Coinage Act, 2011 है। यानी बड़ा coin ढेर लेने की मजबूरी limit पर रुकती है।
beats.on_screen: Prescribed ceiling bounds compulsory acceptance; beyond it acceptance is voluntary
beats.source: Coinage Act, 2011, section 6

beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट नहीं। और खास design से circulation साबित नहीं होता: collector set रोज़ चलने वाला coin नहीं। Valid coins की limit पार करना उनका status खोना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Outside boundaries: legal-tender status ≠ unrestricted transactions or universal retail compulsion. Special design alone ≠ circulation issue; exceeding a ceiling ≠ demonetization
beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Currency Management, 2024; Coinage Act, 2011, section 6; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 269ST, inserted 2017

beats.say: Recognition के बाद अगला सवाल denomination और total limit है: notes की ceiling नहीं, coins की तय है।
beats.on_screen: Legal recognition → next: denomination-specific aggregate limits

beats.say: क्या हर legal tender fiat ही होगा? सामान्य जोड़ ऐसा है, लेकिन universal ‘must’ गलत होगा; Bitcoin exception इसे तोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Fiat: value basis; legal tender: legal status

beats.say: याद में बना हर coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं, लेकिन legal tender हो भी सकते हैं, नहीं भी; अधिकांश होने का मतलब सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग रह सकती हैं।
beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status

beats.say: Pack वाला coin खर्च क्यों नहीं होता? Government Mint collector commemorative coins proof या UNC sets में बेचती है। Proof खास finish, UNC यानी Uncirculated; condition बचाने के लिए daily payments कम होते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Government Mint collector sets: proof finish / uncirculated condition → preservation

beats.say: 4 पुराने 25 paise coins दें तो ₹1 bill चुक जाएगा? दुकानदार मना करे तो ₹1 बाकी रहता है; valid ₹1 coin दें तो बकाया ₹0 होता है। पुराने coins का legal-tender status हटना demonetization है।
beats.on_screen: Four old 25-paise coins refused: debt ₹1 → ₹1; valid ₹1 replacement: debt ₹1 → ₹0

beats.say: Change के डिब्बे में कौन-से coins हैं? ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10, ₹20 को जोड़कर ₹1,000 तक की tender limit है। 50 paise जोड़ें तो ₹10 तक; उससे छोटे coins जोड़ने से legal-tender payment नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Sort change drawer: listed rupee coins → ₹1,000 meter; 50 paise → ₹10 meter; smaller coins → no tender status

beats.say: ₹20 के 50 coins जोड़ें तो ₹1,000 बनते हैं; limit 1,000 coins की नहीं है। 50 paise के 20 coins जोड़ें तो ₹10 बनते हैं; denomination और total limit अलग हैं।
Coinage Act, 2011 के limits में 50 paise अलग है: आधा रुपया, उससे नीचे नहीं। इसलिए पुराने 25 paise से इसे मत मिलाइए। Commemorative coins में ‘most’ यानी सभी नहीं; कोई numerical count भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Coinage Act limits: 50 paise has its own row; 25 paise falls below it; most ≠ all or a numerical count

beats.say: Limit पार करना status खोना नहीं; collector price legal status लौटाती नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Excess amount ≠ demonetization

beats.say: Denomination × count निकालिए; फिर total limit और status जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Total = denomination × count → ceiling + status

beats.say: Phone पर Bitcoin payment दिखे तो government-issued money है? नहीं; El-Salvador का example issuance और legal status अलग करता है।
beats.on_screen: Network issuance ≠ government issuance

beats.say: 2024 तक El-Salvador में Bitcoin non-fiat legal-tender exception था। इसका mechanism अलग समझिए: नए bitcoin mining से network rules पर बनते हैं; price demand-supply से, government के fixed-value promise से नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Historical example: El-Salvador through 2024. Outside explanation: protocol-governed mining; market valuation rather than a sovereign fixed-value promise
beats.source: Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, 2008; IMF, Global Financial Stability Report, Chapter 2, October 2021

beats.say: 2025 reforms के बाद practical compulsory acceptance हटी; ownership और voluntary use legal रहे। दोनों राज़ी हों तो payment संभव है—यह ban नहीं।
beats.on_screen: 2025 practical account: compulsion removed; legal ownership and voluntary use remain

beats.say: कानूनी recognition बदलने से network का issuer government नहीं बनता।
beats.on_screen: Outside distinction: changed payment status ≠ sovereign issuance
beats.source: IMF, Cryptoassets as National Currency? A Step Too Far, 2021

beats.say: अलग पूछिए: issuer कौन, ownership legal, acceptance voluntary या compulsory?
beats.on_screen: Issuer | ownership | acceptance

beats.say: ₹100 silver commemorative coin पर collector कई हज़ार क्यों दे? वही coin payment और collection में अलग role निभाता है।
beats.on_screen: One coin: payment versus collector sale

beats.say: Payment में ₹100; collector sale में कई हज़ार संभव। Face value और market price अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹100 payment value | several-thousand collector price

beats.say: Collector silver, condition और collectability के लिए ज़्यादा देता है; denomination नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Outside explanation: metal and collector attributes can produce a premium without changing face value
beats.source: United States Mint, Coin Collecting Basics, 2024

beats.say: Collector price debt-settlement amount या compulsory coin-payment limit नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Market price ≠ debt discharged ≠ tender ceiling

beats.say: Payment में denomination, collection में agreed price याद रखिए।
beats.on_screen: Payment: denomination | collection: agreed price

beats.say: College की ₹1,000 fees बिना cash कैसे भरें? आपके खाते में ₹2,000 हैं; आप bank को ₹1,000 देने का लिखा instruction देते हैं। Clearing पर bank college को ₹1,000 पहुँचाता है; आपके ₹1,000 बचते हैं। Funds कम हों तो fees बाकी रहती है।
beats.on_screen: Written instruction → successful clearing transfers ₹1,000 from a ₹2,000 deposit → ₹1,000 remains; failed clearing leaves fee unpaid
beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, sections 6 and 31; RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems, 2024

beats.say: दूसरे रास्ते में issuer college को arrangement से payment पहुँचाता है। पहले आपका उससे कोई उधार नहीं था; अब ₹1,000 उसे लौटाने हैं, charges छोड़कर। आपने जमा पैसा नहीं, credit इस्तेमाल किया।
beats.on_screen: Alternative route: issuer settles college payment → student owes issuer ₹1,000; charges and timing simplified
beats.source: RBI, Credit Card and Debit Card—Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022

beats.say: पहला cheque था, दूसरा credit card: दोनों payment instruments हैं। Cheque जमा पैसे का instruction है; card credit तक पहुँच है। College का लेना इन्हें खुद fiat currency या legal tender नहीं बनाता; value का आधार, legal status और payment method अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Cheque: deposit-payment instruction; credit card: access to credit. Accepted instrument ≠ fiat currency or legal-tender status
beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, section 6; RBI, Credit Card and Debit Card—Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022; Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, section 26

beats.say: Value, legal status और payment method अलग हैं। आगे: gold link बिना dollar की माँग क्यों?
beats.on_screen: Value basis ≠ legal status ≠ payment instrument; next: demand for dollars after the gold link

replace_beats.say: ₹100 उधार कैसे चुकाएँ? आप ₹100 valid currency देते हैं; दुकानदार पूरा उधार चुका मानता है। अब ₹0 बाकी हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer pays recognised ₹100 currency → existing ₹100 debt cleared

replace_beats.say: खास design वाला valid ₹10 coin मिले तो? अपना 1 coin देकर ₹10 की चीज़ लेते हैं; पूरी कीमत चुक गई।
replace_beats.on_screen: Customer hands over one illustrative valid ₹10 special-design coin → ₹10 purchase paid

replace_beats.say: Legal tender government से officially recognised money है, जो उसकी territory में debts और transactions चुकाता है। Circulation commemorative coins याद में बने, लेकिन रोज़ ordinary coins जैसे इस्तेमाल होने वाले coins हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Legal recognition; circulation use despite special design

replace_beats.say: Unlimited हर cash transaction की छूट नहीं। खास design circulation साबित नहीं करता; collector set अलग है। Valid coins की limit पार करना status खोना नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Outside boundaries: legal-tender status ≠ unrestricted transactions or universal retail compulsion. Special design alone ≠ circulation issue; exceeding a ceiling ≠ demonetization
replace_beats.source: RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Currency Management, 2024; Coinage Act, 2011, section 6; Income-tax Act, 1961, section 269ST, inserted 2017

replace_beats.say: हर याद वाला coin payment में चलेगा? Commemorative coins fiat issues हैं; अधिकांश legal tender हैं, सभी नहीं। Metal और collector value भी अलग हैं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Commemorative purpose ≠ automatic legal-tender status; check issue conditions; metal and collector value remain separate

replace_beats.say: Coinage Act, 2011 में 50 paise की अलग limit है; इसे छोटे 25 paise से मत मिलाइए। Commemorative coins में ‘most’ सभी नहीं, कोई numerical count भी नहीं।
replace_beats.on_screen: Coinage Act limits: 50 paise has its own row; 25 paise falls below it; most ≠ all or a numerical count

replace_beats.say: ₹1,000 fees बिना cash कैसे दें? खाते के ₹2,000 में से bank को ₹1,000 college पहुँचाने का लिखा instruction देते हैं। Clearing पर college को ₹1,000 मिलते हैं, आपके ₹1,000 बचते हैं। Funds कम हों तो fees बाकी है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Written instruction → successful clearing transfers ₹1,000 from a ₹2,000 deposit → ₹1,000 remains; failed clearing leaves fee unpaid
replace_beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, sections 6 and 31; RBI, Annual Report 2023–24, Payment and Settlement Systems, 2024

replace_beats.say: पहला cheque, दूसरा credit card था: payment instruments, खुद currency नहीं। Cheque deposits का instruction, card credit तक पहुँच है। College का स्वीकार करना fiat या legal-tender status नहीं देता; payment method अलग सवाल है।
replace_beats.on_screen: Cheque: deposit-payment instruction; credit card: access to credit. Accepted instrument ≠ fiat currency or legal-tender status
replace_beats.source: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, section 6; RBI, Credit Card and Debit Card—Issuance and Conduct Directions, 2022; Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, section 26
